title: Cap. VI Arg. 4: from the difference of divine vocation — Jesuits and Arminians forced to grant it
pass_a_gloss: Fourthly, we dispute from the difference of Divine vocation, which the Jesuits themselves and the Arminians are compelled to acknowledge. And so this our reason is instituted: If God calls certain ones with a certain peculiar vocation (which the Apostle, Rom. 8:28, calls vocation according to purpose; which Prosper calls special vocation, On the Calling of the Gentiles 2.23; Augustine, the vocation by which one becomes a believer, On the Predestination of the Saints ch. 16, and vocation according to purpose, by which God fulfills what he predestined, ibid. ch. 17, and hidden grace which is refused by no hard heart, ibid. ch. 8; which finally the Jesuits themselves point out as congruent and high vocation) — if, I say, there is such a vocation of all the elect and of the elect only, then it is clear that God predestined the same with a will antecedent to their foresighted faith.
pass_b_english: Fourth argument: from the difference of divine calling — which even Jesuits and Arminians must grant. If God calls some with a peculiar vocation (Paul's vocation according to purpose, Rom. 8:28; Prosper's special vocation; Augustine's vocation that makes a believer, and vocation according to purpose by which God fulfills what he predestined, and hidden grace no hard heart refuses; the Jesuits' congruent and high vocation) — if that calling is of all the elect and of none but the elect, then God clearly predestined them with a will that goes before any foresight of their faith.
source_text: Quarto, disputamus a discrimine vocationis Divinae, quam ipsi Jesuitas atque Arminiani coguntur agnoscere. Sic autem instituitur haec ratio nostra: Si Deus quosdam vocat peculiari quadam vocatione (quam Apostolus, Rom. viii. 28, vocat vocationem secundum propositum; quam Prosper specialem vocationem, De vocat. Gent. 2. 23; Augustinus, vocationem qua fit credens, De Praed. Sanct. cap. 16, et vocationem secundum propositum, qua Deus implet quod praedestinavit, ibid. cap. 17, et gratiam occultam quae a nullo duro corde respuitur, ibid. cap. 8; quam denique ipsi Jesuitae vocationem congruentem et altam indigitant) — si inquam sit talis omnium electorum et non nisi electorum vocatio, tum clarum est Deum eosdem praedestinasse voluntate praevisam illorum fidem antecedente.
